technical.lead: Great American AI Act draft: 3-year state preemption plus federal rules
technical.body: Representatives Jay Obernolte (R-Calif.) and Lori Trahan (D-Mass.) released a bipartisan discussion draft of the Great American Artificial Intelligence Act on Thursday June 4 - a roughly 270-page text meant to gather stakeholder feedback before formal introduction. The headline provision is a three-year preemption of state laws that specifically regulate the development of frontier AI models (it would block rules like California's AB 2013 training-data-disclosure law and part of SB 942 watermarking, while leaving general-applicability and use/deployment laws intact). In exchange, the draft requires large frontier developers (reported threshold: more than $500 million in prior-year gross revenue) to publish a public frontier AI framework describing how they evaluate and manage catastrophic risks, and codifies the Center for AI Standards and Innovation in Commerce with $100 million a year authorized for fiscal 2027-2029.

technical.lead: CVE-2026-25879: prompt-injection-to-RCE in Langroid SQLChatAgent, CVSS 9.8
technical.body: A new advisory rates CVE-2026-25879 in Langroid - a popular open-source framework for LLM-powered apps - as CVSS 9.8 critical. The flaw lives in the SQLChatAgent, which executes SQL produced by the model; because that SQL is steerable by prompt injection (directly via a malicious prompt or indirectly by poisoning data the model later reads), an attacker can coerce dangerous dialect-specific primitives. When the agent connects with an over-privileged database role (PostgreSQL pg_execute_server_program, MySQL FILE, MSSQL xp_cmdshell), primitives like COPY ... FROM PROGRAM escalate from data theft to remote code execution on the database host. The fix landed in Langroid 0.63.0, which defaults SQLChatAgent to a SELECT-only allowlist parsed with sqlglot plus a dialect-aware dangerous-pattern blocklist.

technical.lead: Exploited LiteLLM proxy SQL injection (CVE-2026-42208) drives access rule
technical.body: The Langroid flaw shares a through-line with the actively exploited LiteLLM proxy injection, CVE-2026-42208, where a crafted Authorization header reached an unparameterized key-lookup query through the error-handling path - fixed in v1.83.7 and recommended at v1.83.10-stable. Both flaws trace the same text-to-SQL-to-database path and underline one lesson: any LLM allowed to author SQL must run against a least-privilege, read-only-by-default database role, because the model's output has to be treated as untrusted, attacker-controllable input.

technical.lead: MiniMax M3 claims open-weight frontier coding, 1M context - no weights yet
technical.body: China's MiniMax launched M3, billed as the first open-weight system to combine frontier coding-agent performance, a one-million-token context window, and native multimodality. The architecture centers on a new MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) mechanism that scores only selected segments to sidestep the quadratic cost of full attention, reaching the 1M-token window; MiniMax says it trained on roughly 100 trillion interleaved text-image tokens with per-token compute about one-twentieth of its prior M2.7. It reports 59.0% on SWE-Bench Pro (ahead of GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, approaching Claude Opus 4.7) and 83.5 on BrowseComp. The key caveat: scores are company-reported, the model is reachable only via MiniMax's API and Code app, and weights plus a technical report are promised on Hugging Face and GitHub within about ten days but have not yet appeared (the newest published checkpoint there is still M2.7).

technical.lead: Bay Area calendar: WWDC26 June 8-12, then Databricks Data + AI Summit June 15-18
technical.body: With Microsoft Build and Snowflake Summit closed, the next still-upcoming Bay Area event to plan around is Apple's WWDC26, running the week of June 8-12 at Apple Park and online - opening Monday June 8 with the keynote at 10:00 AM PT and the Platforms State of the Union at 1:00 PM PT, followed by 100-plus video sessions, with AI-focused Siri and OS updates expected. Next comes Databricks Data + AI Summit, June 15-18 at Moscone, where the company expects 30,000-plus in-person attendees across 800-plus sessions; the keynote lineup includes Ali Ghodsi, Matei Zaharia, a recorded fireside with Satya Nadella, and OpenAI president Greg Brockman, plus a multi-day hackathon run with OpenAI. Further out, the AI Engineer World's Fair runs June 29-July 2 at Moscone West.
